about: The revision language (docs/places/revise-language.md): what a revision of a place can do, step by step. The AI turns the user's words into these instructions; the engine checks each one and runs it on the plan and the layout (PLL). The Build panel lists them as what can be asked.

params.zone: a zone of the place, by its id
params.node: a part of the plan, by its id: a zone, or a parcel inside one (zone/parcel)
params.kind: a kind of parcel the zone may hold (a module id, e.g. house-plot)
params.module: a zone module the place may have (e.g. residential-ward)
params.factor: how many times its size: more than 1 to grow, less than 1 to shrink
params.rel: where it goes: a list of {type, to}; type is one of near, adjacent, along, far, north-of, south-of, east-of, west-of (to a part, the river or a road) or in-north, in-south, in-east, in-west (to site: that part of the map)
params.side: where in its zone: north, south, east, west or middle
params.look: how they look: {field: value} of the kind's settings (e.g. {house-kind: cottage})
params.then: what the other zone does: swap (takes the first one's old land) or place (placed again)
params.path: a Brief setting (e.g. shape.layout, scale.class, components.<id>.assets.variants)

instructions.says: Two zones change places: each takes the other's land exactly.
examples: swap the market and the craftsmen ward
move the farms to where the houses are and the houses to where the farms are

instructions.says: A zone goes where another is now; that one takes its old land (swap) or is placed again (place).
examples: put the temple ward where the market is now

instructions.says: A zone moved by so many cells, keeping its shape. "A little" is about a fifth of its width.
examples: move the docks a little further north
shift the market 10 cells east

instructions.says: A zone placed anew where the words say (beside, north of, along the river, in the west of the map); the zones around it keep their land unless it has no room.
examples: put the temple ward north of the market
move the farms along the river

instructions.says: A zone made bigger where it stands: it spreads from its middle into open land, then into its neighbours'.
examples: make the residential ward bigger
make the craftsmen ward twice as big

instructions.says: A zone made smaller where it stands; it holds fewer buildings in proportion, and the land it gives up is left open.
examples: make the market smaller
halve the outskirts

instructions.says: A new zone, where the words say (or wherever there's room).
examples: add a temple ward east of the market

instructions.says: A zone taken out; its land is left open.
examples: remove the outskirts

instructions.says: A zone held where it is: nothing in this revision moves or shrinks it.
examples: make the market bigger but keep the temple ward where it is

instructions.says: Exactly so many more parcels of a kind in a zone; the other zones don't change. The zone takes the open land beside it if it's full.
examples: add 10 more houses to the residential ward
add 3 workshops to the craftsmen ward

instructions.says: Parcels taken out: so many of a kind from a zone, or one by its id. Nothing else moves.
examples: remove 4 houses from the outskirts
take out the well in ward 1

instructions.says: So many parcels of one kind in a zone turned into another kind (all of them when no count is given).
examples: turn 3 of the houses in the outskirts into farms

instructions.says: One parcel moved: to a side of its zone, beside another parcel, or into another zone.
examples: move the well to the north of ward 1
put the inn next to the market square
move the inn into the market ward

instructions.says: One setting of a zone or a parcel (its street pattern, its house kind…).
examples: give the residential ward a grid of streets
make the houses in ward 2 longhouses

instructions.says: One setting of the whole place: its layout pattern, its size, how its things look.
examples: make it a radial town
use more than one kind of art for the houses
